nina: Noticed a weird failure when using the TS SDK inside Next.js middleware on Vercel preview. Local dev is fine but preview fails with: "TypeError: Response.prototype.arrayBuffer is not a function". Anyone seen something like that?
kevin: Yup. Edge runtime has a constrained Fetch API surface. Sometimes bundlers pull in node-only shims when package.json exports aren't explicit. That can replace globals with polyfills missing some methods.
ash: For us the cause was the SDK's logger importing `util.inspect` (node builtin). SWC bundled it into the edge bundle and then Vercel's runtime threw on the missing methods. We fixed by lazy-importing the node logger behind a runtime check.
ash: Minimal pattern we used:
```js
if (typeof window === 'undefined' && typeof process !== 'undefined') {
  const nodeLogger = await import('./node-logger.js')
  nodeLogger.init()
}
```
nina: That rings true. My middleware imports the SDK at top-level which triggers the logger import. Moving the SDK createClient call inside the function delayed the import and avoided the node-only codepath. But I still get TS errors: "Cannot find name 'Request'".
kevin: Two ways to handle TS: 1) instruct users to extend tsconfig for middleware: set "lib": ["esnext","dom"] in the Next.js middleware tsconfig, or 2) ship an edge.d.ts for the SDK that declares the web globals. We should probably do both.
omar: Also watch out for timers. Edge runtime doesn't have setTimeout in the same way. Our retry implementation used setTimeout+clearTimeout which caused leaks in middleware. Switched to AbortController signal.timeout when available or a micro-debounce using promise.race with manual deadline.
kevin: Important packaging fix: add an explicit `exports` map in package.json so consumers bundling for edge get `./edge` entrypoint instead of default CJS. Example: {"exports": { ".": {"import":"./dist/index.mjs","require":"./dist/index.cjs"},"./edge":"./dist/edge.mjs" } }
nina: Could we also add a nextjs-edge example to examples/ showing proper import patterns and tsconfig tweaks? That would help onboarding.
kevin: Yes — we'll add `examples/nextjs-edge-middleware` showing: - import from 'redwood-inference/edge' - middleware placement (inside function) - tsconfig override - avoiding top-level side effects.
ash: Also, types: avoid referencing NodeJS.Timer or Buffer in base d.ts. Create a minimal web-friendly subset for edge builds.
bot-ci: ci/test:edge-matrix job failed on node 18 matrix run due to missing edge export.
omar: I'll open a tiny patch: 1) move logger behind lazy import, 2) add ./edge export and edge build, 3) add edge.d.ts, 4) add nextjs-edge example. Targetting tomorrow for a patch release.
nina: Great, thanks — I'll validate on our preview once it's up.
